_comment: These do not exist in DROID firmware and are unknown to the Droid Forge.
Schema is the Forge's droidfirmware.json circuit schema, so the same file
feeds BOTH consumers: tools/jackgen/jackgen.py (engine jack tables) and
tools/droidcheck/build.sh (merged into the validator's embedded firmware).
Adding an experimental circuit = one entry here + one engine/circuits/*.cpp.

midihirescc.title: 14-bit (hi-res) MIDI CC output
midihirescc.description: Sends continuous controllers at 14-bit resolution, emitting each MSB/LSB pair atomically from one update. One jack per hi-res-capable controller: hirescc22 drives CC22 (MSB) and CC54 (LSB). USB only.

inputs.name: usb
inputs.description: Number of the USB port to send on, counting the master's own ports first and the X7's after: 1 is the first USB port, 10 means all USB ports, 0 means none. This circuit does not offer TRS output: 14-bit CCs at a useful update rate do not fit through a classical MIDI cable.

inputs.name: channel
inputs.description: MIDI channel to send on, 1 to 16. Both bytes of a pair always go out on this channel.

inputs.name: lsbfirst
inputs.description: Byte order within a pair. Default 1 sends the LSB before the MSB, which is what receivers that keep a single pending-LSB latch need in order to apply the whole 14-bit value at once. Set to 0 for the MIDI specification's MSB-then-LSB order.

inputs.name: updaterate
inputs.description: Maximum number of updates per second and per controller. A controller is sent only when its 14-bit value actually changes, so a still input costs nothing; this caps how often a moving one may be resent. Zero or negative stops all updates.

inputs.name: hirescc1 ... hirescc31
inputs.description: A 14-bit controller. The jack number IS the MIDI controller number of the MSB; the LSB is always that number plus 32, as the MIDI standard defines (hirescc8 sends CC8 and CC40). The value 0.0 to 1.0 is resolved internally to 0 to 16383 and clamped. Controller 0 has no jack: it is Bank Select, and MIDI numbers hi-res controllers from 1 here. Controllers 6 (Data Entry, the payload of RPN/NRPN) and 7 (Volume, which midiout already sends as a 14-bit pair) are available but mean something specific to most receivers.

trigseq.title: Declarative trigger sequencer
trigseq.description: Plays a rhythm written as text: each clock advances one character, '.' ' ' '-' '_' are rests, every other character emits. Chain instances with chaintonext for longer sequences.

inputs.name: clock
inputs.description: Patch a clock signal here. Each trigger advances the pattern by one character. Classified as a gate input: the gate length is preserved when forwarded to output and offbeats.

inputs.name: reset
inputs.description: A trigger here restarts the pattern; the restart is consumed by the next clock.

inputs.name: pattern
inputs.description: The rhythm, as a quoted text. '.', space, '-' and '_' are rests; every other character emits a trigger. The pattern cannot be changed while the patch is running.

inputs.name: outputsignal
inputs.description: Usually trigseq lets the input clock through on active steps. If this parameter is used, its value is sent to the output for the whole active step instead.

inputs.name: chaintonext
inputs.description: If you set this input to 1, the next trigseq circuit's pattern is appended to this one, forming a longer sequence.

outputs.name: output
outputs.description: Emits on active steps. The gate length and voltage are taken from the input clock, unless outputsignal is used.

outputs.name: offbeats
outputs.description: Emits on rest steps — the exact complement of output.

crossfader2.title: Morph between 8 inputs, smoothly
crossfader2.description: crossfader with two extra inputs: curve (0 linear = bit-identical to crossfader, 1 = monotone cubic through the inputs, smooth and never overshooting) and loop (treat the inputs as a ring so fade 0..1 travels through all of them and back to the first).

inputs.name: input1 ... input8
inputs.description: The input signals that you want to crossfade between. At least input1 and input2 need to be patched. Otherwise they are treated like 0 V signals. Exactly as in crossfader.

inputs.name: fade
inputs.description: Position of the morph. At 0.0 the output is 100% of the first input. At 1.0 it is 100% of the last patched input, or, with loop set, back at the first input again. Values beyond 1.0 wrap around from the last input to the first, exactly as in crossfader.

inputs.name: curve
inputs.description: Interpolation between two neighbouring inputs. 0 = linear, bit-identical to crossfader. 1 = cubic: a monotone cubic curve that passes exactly through every input value, has a continuous slope across the inputs, and never overshoots the range between two neighbouring inputs.

inputs.name: loop
inputs.description: When set, the inputs form a ring: fade 0.0 ... 1.0 travels through all N patched inputs and back to the first one in N equal segments, so a sawtooth at fade gives a seamless cyclic morph. When off, fade 0.0 ... 1.0 travels from the first to the last input in N-1 segments, exactly as in crossfader.
